\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-99},
  title = {Prometheus, cAdvisor and node-exporter run in every stack, with no public port},
  date = {2026-11-04},
  milestone = {M6: Monitoring},
  topic = {Monitoring, Containerization},
  participants = {Lukas Häußler (decided), AI agents (architecture proposal, implementation)},
  decision = {Prometheus scrapes the API, cAdvisor (per container) and node-exporter (the host) every 15 s inside the Compose network and keeps at most 2 GB or 60 days.
None publishes a port, and all always run, without a Compose profile.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item node-exporter only: no container's memory against its limit, and no restarts.
\item cAdvisor only: a weak view of the host's disk, which NFR-04's 4 GB floor is about.
\item A Compose profile: CI, laptops, and the VM would run different stacks.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} NFR-04 limits each container and the disk, and each exporter covers one of them.
The VM's ports 8080 to 8089 are public, so nothing new is published.
The three used 79 MiB of their 640 MiB of limits on a laptop.
cAdvisor runs as root with the Docker socket, the tested exception to the shared hardening.},
  ai = {Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation, Solution generation},
